transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I can’t stop getting stuck on these awful ‘what if I missed something’ thoughts about my design files, and they’re taking over my workday. It’s like my brain just won't let me move past them, and it's making it incredibly hard to actually get any work done.
When you have these thoughts about missing something, do you feel an overwhelming urge to repeatedly check or redo your design files to make the anxiety go away?

Yes, I do, and it's exhausting. I end up reopening the same files over and over, zooming in on every line of text and re-exporting the artwork just to try to calm the panic. I can spend hours doing this, but even after all that checking, it never actually feels safe to send to the client.
Do you find yourself constantly worrying about many different areas of your life, like your health, family, or finances, or is this intense anxiety and checking mostly focused on your work?

It is almost entirely focused on my design work and files, like worrying about typos or color codes, rather than things like my health or finances. Even though this anxiety has ruined my personal life—making me skip gardening and seeing friends because I'm so behind—the actual worry is strictly about making a mistake on a project. I just can't shake the fear that a small oversight will ruin a client's business and my reputation.
Do you feel, deep down, that this level of worry and repetitive checking is excessive or unreasonable, even if you feel powerless to stop it?

Yes, absolutely, and it's incredibly frustrating because intellectually I know it is completely excessive, especially after I've already checked the files multiple times. But even though I know it makes no sense, I still feel completely powerless to stop that overwhelming 'what if' anxiety and the urge to keep rechecking.

latest_inference.note: The patient exhibits classic symptoms of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (F42), including ego-dystonic obsessive thoughts ('what if I missed something' in design files) and compulsive checking behaviors (reopening, zooming, re-exporting files for hours) that cause significant impairment in social and occupational functioning. General anxiety disorder is ruled out as the worry is strictly focused on these obsessions. There is sufficient evidence to finalize the diagnosis of F42.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with classic symptoms of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (ICD-10: F42), characterized by persistent, intrusive thoughts about making mistakes in design files (obsessions) and repetitive, time-consuming checking behaviors (compulsions) performed to alleviate anxiety. The patient recognizes these thoughts and behaviors as excessive and unreasonable (ego-dystonic). The symptoms cause significant functional impairment, including falling behind on work and withdrawing from social and leisure activities. Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1) was considered but ruled out because the anxiety and worry are strictly circumscribed to the obsessive themes of design errors and the associated compulsive checking, rather than being generalized across multiple life domains.
